key_insight: ContiLNN adds bidirectional continuous-time slice modeling to 2D medical image restoration so the model can use cross-slice anatomy while adapting to variable slice spacing.
clinical_relevance: It may improve restoration quality for CT, MRI, and PET images when slice sampling is irregular, which could support clearer downstream interpretation.
method: Wraps a 2D restoration backbone with Bi-CfC modules for bidirectional cross-slice propagation.
Uses slice-interval-gated updates driven by local features and hidden states to handle sampling gaps without ODE solving.
Adds reference-guided consistency loss and distillation from a frozen backbone to preserve anatomical variation and in-plane fidelity.
evidence_signal: Across five seeds, ContiLNN improved mean PSNR over Restore-RWKV and reduced RMSE on CT denoising, MRI super-resolution, and reduced-count PET restoration; profiling also showed lower latency and GPU memory than a Bi-GRU.
watch_item: Results include descriptive CT evaluation for one held-out patient and performance varies with sampling context, so generalization to other datasets and acquisition patterns needs caution.
paper_title: ContiLNN: Mitigating Slice Sampling Discontinuity with Liquid Neural Networks for Medical Image Restoration
